title: IoT-Oriented Security for Small Sensor Systems Using DnCNN Denoising and Multimodal Feature Fusion for Image Forgery Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: Sections 3.1 and 6.1 and Table 2 evaluate CASIA 2.0 for conventional splicing, copy-move, and compositing detection/localization; Section 6.2 identifies GenImage and diffusion-era evaluation only as future work.
mechanism: Passive classical image-manipulation detection and localization from denoising, noise-residual, texture, and structural cues.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: No substantive modern generative-image experiment is reported; GenImage and diffusion evaluation are future work only.
rationale: The evaluated contribution is classical-only image manipulation forensics, so it conflicts with the current narrowed synthetic-image scope while remaining a legitimate legacy inclusion under the earlier policy.

title: Copy-Move Forgery Detection (CMFD) Using Deep Learning for Image and Video Forensics
decisive_datasets_tasks: Section 3 and Tables 3-5 evaluate eight open-access classical copy-move datasets; Sections 4.1 and 6 define and assess only copy-move forgery detection.
mechanism: Passive classical copy-move forgery detection with custom and transfer-learning convolutional models.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: No fully generated, diffusion-edited, or other modern generative-image benchmark is evaluated.
rationale: The paper's experiments are limited to classical copy-move manipulation, which is outside the current narrowed scope.

title: DeepFake Image Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The accessible primary abstract describes a comparison of ResNet, InceptionV3, and DenseNet for deepfake image and face-forgery detection, but it does not name the experimental datasets or establish the evaluated manipulation classes.
mechanism: Passive CNN-based deepfake image detection; the benchmark's face-only or broader scope remains unverified.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: No accessible primary dataset or experimental section establishes independent evaluation of broader fully generated or generatively edited images.
exact_evidence_needed: Which named datasets and manipulation classes are used in the primary experiments, and do they substantively include broader fully generated or generatively edited images beyond face-only deepfakes?
rationale: The title, taxonomy, keywords, and abstract cannot determine whether the evaluated images are face-only or broader synthetic imagery without the primary experimental details.

title: AdaptPrompt: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of VLMs for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
decisive_datasets_tasks: The experimental dataset section introduces the balanced 200,000-image Diff-Gen corpus, including 100,000 diffusion-generated images across 20 LSUN categories, and the evaluation tables test generalization across 25 GAN, diffusion, and commercial generators.
mechanism: Passive general synthetic-image detection using parameter-efficient visual-language-model prompt adaptation.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: Substantive independent experiments cover diverse non-face object and scene categories and multiple GAN, diffusion, and commercial image generators.
rationale: The primary experiments directly evaluate broad AI-generated imagery rather than a face-only or video-only deepfake task.

title: EKILA: Synthetic Media Provenance and Attribution for Generative Art
decisive_datasets_tasks: Sections 4.1-4.3 and Table 1 evaluate passive query-to-training-image attribution with a 10-million-image LAION corpus plus 40 latent-diffusion queries and a 1-million-image IPF-Stock corpus plus 60 latent-diffusion queries using R@1, R@5, R@10, and mAP; Section 4.4 separately evaluates DreamBooth attribution.
mechanism: Passive visual attribution from naturally occurring image similarity traces, combined with a separable C2PA/NFT provenance and rights framework.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: The paper contains a substantive, independently evaluated passive synthetic-image attribution contribution despite its additional active-provenance infrastructure.
rationale: Its passive image-to-training-source attribution experiments satisfy the current source-attribution scope independently of the C2PA and tokenized-rights components.

title: Evading Watermark based Detection of AI-Generated Content
decisive_datasets_tasks: Section 7 trains and attacks HiDDeN and UDH embedded-bit watermark systems on COCO, ImageNet, and Conceptual Captions and evaluates a Stable Diffusion system carrying an intentionally embedded 136-bit watermark.
mechanism: Active watermark detection and watermark-evasion analysis against intentionally embedded signals.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: The experiments do not establish an independent passive detector based on naturally occurring generator traces.
rationale: The contribution studies evasion of active watermark-based detection, which falls outside the current passive synthetic-image forensic scope.

title: AI-generated Image Detection: Passive or Watermark?
decisive_datasets_tasks: Table 1 and Sections 4-6 benchmark Stable Diffusion 2.1, DALL-E 3, DeepFloyd IF, and Hunyuan-DiT imagery and independently report five passive detectors under cross-dataset evaluation, common perturbations, and adversarial perturbations.
mechanism: Comparative benchmark of passive synthetic-image detectors and active watermark detectors.
broader_synthetic_image_evidence: The five passive detectors receive substantive independent evaluation on four fully generated-image datasets, separate from the watermark systems.
rationale: The independently evaluated passive-forensics branch directly satisfies the current synthetic-image detection scope even though the benchmark also evaluates watermark systems.
